title: Resolver chaining and iptables egress guardrails (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for handling private DNS resolution across VPC and on-prem deployments while enforcing egress guardrails via iptables-based egress gateways. The goal is to provide a reproducible Terraform pattern, an incremental upgrade plan for existing private deployments, and a testing checklist for safe rollouts.

Context and motivation:
- Customers often deploy Redwood Private into VPCs or on-prem networks that require split-horizon DNS (internal names resolve to private addresses) while still accessing external services (package repos, model fetch, monitoring).
- We see two recurring risks: DNS leakage (private hostnames resolving publicly) and incorrect NAT/conntrack behavior that breaks model-serving sessions (long-lived KV cache / streaming token flows).
- Many on-prem environments rely on iptables NAT and do not have cloud managed egress gateways. We need a clear, minimal pattern that ops teams can adopt.

Design summary (high level):
1) Resolver chaining: local node-level stub resolver -> internal forwarder (per-cluster) -> customer upstream or on-prem internal resolvers. Use conditional forwarding for split-horizon zones.
2) Egress gateway: an iptables- and nftables-ready VM or pod acting as a centralized egress point. Apply DNAT/SNAT rules to ensure stable source IPs and connection tracking tuned for long-lived streaming.
3) Terraform modules: small composable modules: dns-forwarder, egress-gateway, firewall-allowlist, conntrack-tuning. Each module has clear inputs/outputs and minimal privileges.

Detailed components:
- Node stub resolver: systemd-resolved or dnsmasq configured to forward unknown zones to cluster-forwarder (127.0.0.1:53). Keep caching TTLs short for dynamic environments (default 30s for service discovery zones, 300s for infra zones).

- Cluster forwarder (recommended): lightweight forwarder (dnsmasq/unbound) running as a DaemonSet or single HA pair in control plane. Responsibilities:
  - Conditional forwarding for zones like internal.redwood.local -> internal resolver IPs
  - Forward all other queries to customer-managed resolvers or public resolvers based on policy
  - Expose metrics (query rates / errors) for SLA tracking

- Split-horizon handling: prefer delegation over host-file hacks. Where delegation isn't possible, implement validation step in Terraform: ensure that the delegated zone is covered and that there are no public authoritative records for the same FQDN.

- Egress NAT behavior and iptables pattern:
  - Use SNAT with a small pool of stable egress IPs (avoid MASQUERADE where possible) so downstream services can whitelist addresses.
  - Preserve source port where possible for better conntrack behavior — set iptables MASQUERADE only for fallback scenarios.
  - Tune conntrack timeouts for TCP_ESTABLISHED and related states to accommodate long streaming sessions (example: increase tcp timeout to 1h for streaming user sessions).
  - Pin ephemeral port ranges to a documented window to help downstream firewalls.

Terraform module notes (snippet-level guidance):
- dns-forwarder module variables:
  - name_prefix (string)
  - forward_zones (list of strings)  // zone -> ip mapping passed as map in var or file
  - node_port (number, default 53)
  - metrics_enabled (bool)
  - health_check_path (string)
- outputs: forwarder_ip, service_account_id, config_map_id

- egress-gateway module variables:
  - egress_ip_pool (list of cidr or ip)
  - mode (string: "vm" | "pod")
  - nat_strategy (string: "snat_pool" | "masquerade")
  - conntrack_params (map of string -> string)
  - firewall_allowlist (list of cidr)

Implementation guidance (examples):
- When mode == "pod" prefer hostNetwork:false and hostPort mapping for observability; run as DaemonSet only in dedicated egress nodes to avoid noisy neighbors.
- Use iptables-save and restore via Terraform provisioners sparingly — prefer a configuration-management approach (cloud-init, userdata, or initContainers).

Upgrade plan (safe path for existing customers):
Phase 0 - baseline audit (low risk):
  - Inventory current resolvers, current NAT behavior, conntrack settings, and existing firewall rules.
  - Run lightweight traffic capture to identify long-lived flows.
Phase 1 - deploy passive forwarder (read-only)
  - Provision forwarder(s) that mirror answers but do not intercept traffic. Compare logs for mismatches.
Phase 2 - enable forwarding for internal zones only
  - Switch nodes to point at local stub resolver that forwards to cluster forwarder. Monitor cache hit rates and query failures.
Phase 3 - egress gateway rollout in "monitor" mode
  - Route traffic through the egress gateway but do not enforce SNAT (keep original source via routing). Collect metrics and stress test streaming endpoints.
Phase 4 - enable SNAT with small egress IP pool and firewall allowlist
  - Validate stability and rollback plan.

Rollback and testing checklist:
- Preflight tests: zone resolution matrix (public vs private FQDNs), TCP streaming benchmark, conntrack utilization under synthetic load
- Post-deploy checks: latency to model fetch endpoints, rate of NAT connection resets, DNS SERVFAIL occurrences
- Quick rollback knobs: switch node resolvers back to customer upstream (DNS TTLs low), disable SNAT on egress gateway, and reassign routes.

Operational runbooks (short):
- On DNS SERVFAIL spikes: check cluster-forwarder logs, check upstream reachability, temporarily set forwarder into transparent-forward mode to bypass policy, notify customer NOC.
- On conntrack exhaustion: increase conntrack max via sysctl, identify noisy pods via netstat on egress gateway, throttle large-socket apps or move to dedicated egress pods.

Security & compliance notes:
- Only allow DNS over TLS (DoT) or DNS over HTTPS (DoH) for upstream resolvers when customer policy requires egress encryption.
- Audit logs: capture resolver query logs for zone delegation validation but mask PII (do not store user prompts).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Define recommended conntrack settings per model size and expected concurrent streaming sessions (need empirical data).
- Decide default TTLs by zone type (service discovery vs infra) and expose as module config.
- Converge on one reference implementation for egress in cloud vs on-prem (current PRs present both approaches).

References and artifacts:
- See linked Confluence doc for background architecture diagrams.
- Terraform reference PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules/pull/214
- Jira ticket for rollout automation: NET-482

Notes to self: keep this document lightweight and actionable. Next step: prototype conntrack settings with realistic streaming workload and add result table here.
